title: General NP witness encryption from plain LWE
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Construct polynomial-time WE for every NP relation from standard decisional LWE alone, specifying modulus, noise, and hardness parameters without evasive or knowledge assumptions.
status: Central frontier since 2013. Evasive-LWE candidates and special-language lattice schemes do not settle it.
why: Gives general encrypt-to-condition a widely studied lattice foundation.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), [Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258); Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs (2022), [Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140).

title: Polynomial-hardness-only algebraic WE
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Obtain general WE from polynomial-hardness versions of DLIN, large-field LPN, and binary sparse LPN, eliminating subexponential hardness without exponential algorithmic overhead.
status: Proposed weakening of the assumptions underlying the 2024 algebraic iO construction.
why: Reduces assumption strength and security-parameter inflation.
key_works: Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).

title: Witness encryption from one-way functions
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Construct general WE from arbitrary one-way functions, potentially using their code non-black-box, or establish a suitably qualified barrier beyond existing black-box separations.
status: Discussed since 2013. WE together with one-way functions already implies public-key encryption.
why: Connects conditional encryption to minimal conventional computational secrecy assumptions.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), [Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258).

title: Perfect correctness from negligible decryption error
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Give an assumption-preserving compiler from negligibly incorrect WE to perfectly correct WE, or prove a barrier for a specified complete NP relation.
status: Outside the scope of the March 2026 equivalence; repetition reduces error without eliminating it.
why: Prevents exceptional encryption randomness from permanently stranding valid rewards or archives.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Remove special-honest-verifier simulation
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Determine whether logarithmic-prover-communication ordinary HVZK arguments imply WE without simulation conditioned on a supplied verifier random tape.
status: The 2026 equivalence uses SHVZK; ordinary HVZK is explicitly distinguished.
why: Could unlock WE from a wider collection of zero-knowledge protocols.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Tight quantitative laconic-to-WE transformations
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Improve the dependence of encryption cost, ciphertext size, and security loss on transcript support and soundness gap, ideally approaching unavoidable input and output costs.
status: Proposed quantitative target beyond the polynomial-equivalence theorem.
why: Determines whether proof-system characterizations can become useful constructions.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: All-length public-key encryption from weak NP hardness and WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Upgrade infinitely-often public-key encryption obtained from nonuniform WE and NP⊄BPP to security at every sufficiently large length under the same premises.
status: The cited route yields infinitely-often security; stronger hardness premises support stronger conclusions.
why: Converts sparse-length cryptographic existence into conventional deployable asymptotics.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2025), [A Note on Zero-Knowledge for NP and One-Way Functions](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/095/revision/2/download).

title: Complete characterization of zero-test leakage
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Characterize algebraic information exposed by all legal zero tests in proposed WE encodings, including combinations lacking low-level zero encodings.
status: Attacks since 2015 show that eliminating obvious zero encodings is insufficient.
why: Replaces patch-by-patch defenses with an explicit leakage boundary.
key_works: Coron et al. (2015), [Zeroizing Without Low-Level Zeroes: New MMAP Attacks and Their Limitations](https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/596); Cheon et al. (2015), [Cryptanalysis on the Multilinear Map over the Integers and its Related Problems](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/906).

title: Better exponents for nontrivial exponential WE
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Improve encryption-time exponents for standard-assumption WE that beats brute-force witness enumeration, preserving the claimed nontriviality regime.
status: Nontrivial exponential-time constructions exist from 2018; polynomial time is a different frontier.
why: May enable bounded-size applications before fully efficient general WE.
key_works: Brakerski–Jain–Komargodski–Passelègue–Wichs (2018), [Non-Trivial Witness Encryption and Null-iO from Standard Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/874).

title: Annihilating FHE without the ideal-cipher model
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Instantiate the annihilating-FHE route to WE in the standard model while retaining its required security properties.
status: Proposed model-removal target following the 2020/2021 construction framework.
why: Replaces an idealized component with an explicit assumption and implementation.
key_works: Kluczniak (2020/2021), [Witness Encryption from Garbled Circuit and Multikey Fully Homomorphic Encryption Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1502).

title: KZG-opening EWE outside the algebraic group model
subfield: Special languages, commitments, and SNARK gadgets
open: Prove comparably efficient EWE for KZG openings in a concrete-group model without adversarial algebraic-representation access.
status: The 2024 construction gives a one-group-element ciphertext in its algebraic model.
why: Strengthens the foundation of one of the most efficient special-language examples.
key_works: Fleischhacker–Hall-Andersen–Simkin (2024), [Extractable Witness Encryption for KZG Commitments and Efficient Laconic OT](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/264).

title: WE gadgets for nonlinear verifiers
subfield: Special languages, commitments, and SNARK gadgets
open: Build efficient WE gadgets covering nonlinear verifier relations without replacing their difficult portions by interaction or general iO.
status: The 2025/2026 framework handles linearly verifiable SNARK structure; nonlinear parts remain consequential.
why: Broadens practical proof-conditioned encryption.
key_works: Garg–Hajiabadi–Kolonelos–Kothapalli–Policharla (2025/2026), [A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364).

title: Remove short-solution promises without stronger knowledge assumptions
subfield: Special languages, commitments, and SNARK gadgets
open: Remove restrictive homogeneous short-solution promises from special-language lattice EWE while retaining a defensible assumption of comparable strength.
status: The 2022–2023 constructions supply important restricted baselines.
why: Makes lattice WE apply to naturally generated instances.
key_works: Choi–Vaudenay (2022), [Towards Witness Encryption Without Multilinear Maps](https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/295725/files/978-3-031-08896-4_2.pdf); Tran–Vaudenay (2023), [Extractable Witness Encryption for the Homogeneous Linear Equations Problem](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-41326-1_9).

title: UP witness PRFs without evasive LWE
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Replace the evasive-LWE premise in the UP route with a well-studied falsifiable assumption.
status: Proposed foundation repair made more pressing by 2025 private-coin counterexamples.
why: Preserves the unique-witness strategy under a more stable assumption base.
key_works: Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227); Döttling et al. (2025), [Simple and General Counterexamples for Private-Coin Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/374).

title: Bounded-ambiguity witness PRFs
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Extend unique-witness constructions to relations with a bounded number of witnesses while preserving a witness-independent output.
status: Proposed intermediate expressivity target between UP and unrestricted NP.
why: Covers naturally ambiguous credentials and proofs.
key_works: Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227).

title: Polynomial-loss adaptive UP arguments
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Replace exponential security loss in the relevant UP argument route with a polynomial-loss reduction.
status: Proposed quantitative improvement to the 2024 framework.
why: Avoids requiring disproportionate underlying hardness.
key_works: Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227).

title: Delegatable witness PRFs below iO
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Delegate restricted public evaluation authority with compact descendant keys and collusion resistance under assumptions below general iO.
status: Proposed extension of WPRFs and constrained evaluation.
why: Supports hierarchical agent and organizational capabilities.
key_works: Zhandry (2014/2016), [How to Avoid Obfuscation Using Witness PRFs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/301).

title: Adaptive offline WE from plain WE and LWE
subfield: Offline, batched, positional, and signature-based WE
open: Obtain fully adaptive offline WE from plain WE plus LWE with near-linear online work and explicit preprocessing amortization.
status: Semi-adaptive and adaptive offline results exist under their respective premises; this combined assumption-and-cost target is stronger.
why: Makes previously unknown conditions cheap to encrypt after preprocessing.
key_works: Pal–Dutta (2020), [Semi-Adaptively Secure Offline Witness Encryption from Puncturable Witness PRF](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/479); Liu et al. (2023), [适应性安全的离线证据加密](https://www.jos.org.cn/jos/article/abstract/6423).

title: QCMA-WE without full QMA machinery
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Construct WE for classical witnesses checked by quantum verifiers from post-quantum NP-WE and weaker additions than general quantum obfuscation.
status: Proposed intermediate model; classical witness strings do not turn quantum verification into an NP relation.
why: Covers a potentially easier and useful quantum-verification class.
key_works: Bartusek–Malavolta (2022), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation of Null Quantum Circuits and Applications](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2022.15).

title: Remove subexponential FE from the QPrO route
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Derive sufficient quantum null obfuscation or QMA-WE in QPrO from polynomially secure functional encryption with polynomial reduction loss.
status: The existing ideal-obfuscation theorem assumes subexponentially secure FE.
why: Reduces the quantitative strength of the underlying premise.
key_works: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Statistical quantum-WE language classification
subfield: Quantum language classes and witness resources
open: Characterize promise languages admitting statistical quantum WE, separately for classical and quantum ciphertexts and efficient quantum samplers.
status: Proposed classification; consequences of general statistical quantum obfuscation do not automatically characterize weaker WE.
why: Identifies information-theoretically secure quantum conditions.
key_works: Alagic–Fefferman (2016), [On Quantum Obfuscation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.01771); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/).

title: The Minicrypt range-avoidance conjecture
subfield: Further named complexity conjectures
open: Prove that one-way functions and NP≠coNP imply Avoid∉FP, where Avoid must output a string outside a stretching circuit’s range. A proposed route replaces strong-WE-derived predictable arguments with sufficient arguments from one-way functions alone.
status: Explicit Conjecture 5.1 of Ren–Wang–Zhong, revised March 2026. Strong-WE and demi-bit results provide partial foundations; the one-way-function premise remains unresolved.
why: Would connect minimal cryptographic hardness to explicit search and proof-complexity consequences.
key_works: Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061); Faonio–Nielsen–Venturi (2017), [Predictable Arguments of Knowledge](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-54365-8_6).

title: Fully succinct cutoff-iO from rate-one null-iO
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: Build cutoff-iO with output length polynomial in \(\lambda\), circuit size, and \(\log N\), assuming rate-one null-iO and LWE. Eliminate multiplicative growth of function-binding hash keys and openings across recursion levels.
status: Explicit open problem in Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026). Substituting rate-one null-iO into their compiler still permits only constantly many recursion levels.
why: Separates a compiler obstacle from the independent construction of rate-one null-iO.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).

title: Fully adaptive circuit registered ABE from plain WE
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Upgrade registered ABE for polynomial-size circuits from plain WE and LWE to adaptive security with polynomial reduction loss, allowing corruption choices to depend on public parameters and previous registrations, including admissible later corruption of honest users. Preserve succinct master and helper keys; adaptive challenge-policy selection alone is insufficient.
status: Proposed strengthening of Freitag–Waters–Wu (2023). The 2026 comparison still classifies this WE-based construction as static; adaptive ordinary broadcast encryption was separately achieved in 2025.
why: Supports securely changing registered populations and adversarial compromise after deployment.
key_works: Cody Freitag, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812); Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Adaptive linear-CRS pairing registered ABE in the plain model
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Obtain fully adaptive registered ABE for monotone span programs with an \(O(N)\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) CRS under polynomially hard, explicitly stated pairing assumptions, without random oracles. Avoid an a priori policy-size bound introduced solely by complexity leveraging.
status: Proposed gap after Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026): linear-CRS static security is proved in the plain model, while the adaptive variant adds random oracles, a policy bound, and subexponential hardness.
why: Combines setup savings with adaptive security under weaker quantitative premises.
key_works: Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-35367-2_13); [full version](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Multi-authority registered ABE from plain WE
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Construct multi-authority registered ABE for general polynomial-size monotone circuits and an a priori unbounded registered population from ordinary WE plus LWE. Preserve independent curators, transparent aggregation, and resistance to combining different users’ attributes across authorities.
status: Proposed assumption-reduction target following Lu–Waters–Wu (2025). Their unbounded expressive construction uses iO and function-binding hashes; their pairing construction bounds the population and supports linear-secret-sharing policies.
why: Extends encrypt-to-condition across autonomous organizations without centralizing key issuance.
key_works: George Lu, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2025), [Multi-Authority Registered Attribute-Based Encryption](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1279); Freitag–Waters–Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812).

title: Public verification from designated-verifier witness maps
subfield: Witness maps, witness PRFs, and proof canonicalization
open: Derive publicly verifiable unique witness maps for NP from witness PRFs, with computational soundness, or separate the primitives. The output must depend only on the statement although evaluation receives an arbitrary valid witness.
status: Proposed converse in the 2023 implication map: public unique witness maps imply WPRFs, while designated-verifier unique witness maps are equivalent to WPRFs.
why: Turns witness-gated pseudorandom evaluation into canonical proofs checkable by anyone.
key_works: Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343).
aliases: WPRF-to-UWM implication; publicizing designated-verifier unique witness maps.

title: Negligible-error canonicalization of compact witness maps
subfield: Witness maps, witness PRFs, and proof canonicalization
open: Convert witness maps with at most \(2^{O(\log\lambda)}\) possible outputs per statement into pseudo-unique witness maps with negligible canonical-output failure and polynomial setup/evaluation. Include setup-dependent failures that repetition under one CRS cannot remove.
status: Proposed quantitative strengthening of Chakraborty–Prabhakaran–Wichs (2023), whose conversion achieves success \(1-1/p(\lambda)\) for any chosen polynomial \(p\).
why: Supports canonical evidence reused across many conditional-encryption applications without fixing an inverse-polynomial error budget.
key_works: Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343).

title: Mildly compact witness maps from ordinary NIZKs
subfield: Witness maps, witness PRFs, and proof canonicalization
open: Determine whether ordinary NIZK arguments for NP and one-way functions suffice for deterministic witness maps with at most \(2^{p(\lambda)}\) outputs per statement, where fixed polynomial \(p\) is independent of statement and witness lengths. Give a construction or an appropriate separation.
status: Proposed converse gap in the 2023 hierarchy: SNARGs imply mildly compact witness maps, which imply NIZKs. Ordinary randomized NIZKs do not establish the required output bound.
why: Locates the assumption strength of compressing witness diversity without requiring short proofs.
key_works: Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343).

title: WE-to-universal-SNARG without short correctness proofs
subfield: Proof-based witness encryption and proof complexity
open: Remove the requirement that the underlying WE has a sufficiently short Extended Frege correctness proof in the universal-SNARG route, retaining explicitly stated auxiliary FHE and batch-argument assumptions. Alternatively, establish a barrier separating arbitrary WE from the required proof-friendly subclass.
status: Proposed strengthening of Jin–Kalai–Lombardi–Mathialagan (2024/2025). Their transparent-CRS nonadaptive universal construction requires suitably EF-friendly WE.
why: Makes a major WE consequence depend on cryptographic functionality rather than the proof complexity of its correctness.
key_works: Zhengzhong Jin, Yael Tauman Kalai, Alex Lombardi, Surya Mathialagan (2025), [Universal SNARGs for NP from Proofs of Correctness](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2015); [DOI 10.1145/3717823.3718104](https://doi.org/10.1145/3717823.3718104).

title: Silent threshold batched IBE without tag-use restrictions
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Build threshold batched IBE with independently generated participant keys, deterministic public aggregation, and compact ciphertexts and decryption keys, allowing polynomially many overlapping release sets without fixing a query bound in setup. Keep parameters independent of the number of releases.
status: Explicit direction in Gong–Waters–Wee–Wu’s May 2026 talk. Silent setup with tag restrictions exists; later multi-key-per-label work improves reuse with setup depending on a query bound.
why: Supports changing encrypted transaction pools and release committees without interactive rekeying.
key_works: Junqing Gong, Brent Waters, Hoeteck Wee, David J. Wu (2026), [Threshold Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Pairings in the Plain Model](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2103), [May 2026 slides](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/talks/BatchDecryption0526.pdf); Guru-Vamsi Policharla (2026), [Labeled Multi-Key Batched IBE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1452).

title: A concrete attack frontier for HLE witness encryption
subfield: Hidden-order witness languages and concrete cryptanalysis
open: Publish reproducible homogeneous-linear-equation WE challenges varying integer-kernel dimension, coefficient size, witness bounds, and hidden-order parameters, then measure combined lattice and number-theoretic attacks. Identify parameter regions surviving both short-solution and order-recovery approaches at explicitly costed security levels.
status: Proposed experimental program. Tran–Vaudenay (2023) repair earlier small-solution issues and construct extractable HLE-WE using hidden-order and knowledge assumptions; no comparable independent attack frontier was located for this census.
why: Tests the specialized construction’s concrete security before practical optimization.
key_works: Bénédikt Tran, Serge Vaudenay (2023), [Extractable Witness Encryption for the Homogeneous Linear Equations Problem](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-41326-1_9).

title: Subquadratic adaptive secret-sharing compilation
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Convert any statically secure computational secret-sharing scheme into an adaptively secure scheme with at most \(O(n\operatorname{polylog}n)\) multiplicative share overhead, preserving the access policy and assumptions. Alternatively, establish a black-box lower bound excluding this target.
status: Quantitative frontier beyond Lu–Waters (2025), whose generic compiler already achieves adaptive security with \(O(n^2)\) overhead.
why: Makes WE-derived access structures usable against adaptive compromise without a quadratic size penalty.
key_works: George Lu, Brent Waters (2025), [How to Make Any Computational Secret Sharing Scheme Adaptively Secure](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1014).

title: Adaptive succinct sharing without full iO
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: For a monotone circuit \(C\) on \(n\) parties, achieve private shares of \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n)\) bits and public information of \(n\operatorname{polylog}n+\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|C|)\) bits, with adaptive privacy, from ordinary WE and LWE. Count all per-secret public information.
status: Proposed combination of two narrower advances: Lu–Nassar–Waters give \(\lambda\)-bit private shares and \(n+\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|C|)\) public bits from iO and injective OWFs; Lu–Waters add generic adaptivity with quadratic overhead.
why: Separates complex authorization policies from the size of their secret shares.
key_works: George Lu, Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters (2025/2026), [Succinct Computational Secret Sharing for Monotone Circuits](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/850); Lu–Waters (2025), [How to Make Any Computational Secret Sharing Scheme Adaptively Secure](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1014).

title: Monotone-P to monotone-NP sharing completeness
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Determine whether efficient sharing for every monotone polynomial-time access structure implies efficient sharing for all monotone NP access structures through a black-box transformation, allowing explicitly stated OWFs. Give a transformation or oracle separation.
status: Explicitly posed by Komargodski–Naor–Yogev in 2014. Their completeness theorem starts with an NP-complete access structure; recent adaptivity and succinctness compilers do not provide the complexity-class lift.
why: Determines whether efficiently deciding authorization already contains the power to encrypt to arbitrary NP witnesses.
key_works: Ilan Komargodski, Moni Naor, Eylon Yogev (2014/2017), [Secret-Sharing for NP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5698).

title: Perfect-matching access structures from OWFs
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Construct polynomial-size computational secret sharing from OWFs alone when parties represent edges and authorized coalitions contain a perfect matching. Bound private shares, public data, dealer work, and reconstruction work polynomially in graph size and security parameter.
status: Longstanding special-access-structure target. WE plus OWFs gives conditional feasibility, while polynomial-time matching does not itself supply a polynomial-size monotone-circuit implementation.
why: Tests how much obfuscation-like power authorization beyond monotone circuits requires.
key_works: Komargodski–Naor–Yogev (2014/2017), [Secret-Sharing for NP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5698); Amos Beimel (2025), [Secret-Sharing Schemes for General Access Structures: An Introduction](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/518).

title: Upgrade classical-advice EWE to quantum auxiliary states
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: Determine whether post-quantum EWE secure with classical auxiliary strings can be upgraded to security with one copy of an efficiently jointly generated quantum auxiliary state, without strengthening its knowledge assumption.
status: Proposed compiler-or-separation target. Quantum-auxiliary EWE is assumed in 2020–2021 unclonable-decryption constructions; quantum computation with classical advice does not establish that premise.
why: Identifies the assumption actually required by quantum-token applications of classical WE.
key_works: Marios Georgiou, Mark Zhandry (2020), [Unclonable Decryption Keys](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/877).

title: Constructive adaptive reductions from quantum WE distinguishers
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: For adaptive classical reductions with polynomial-size solution spaces, characterize when a quantum compiler can use only the original auxiliary state with polynomial overhead and no resampling oracle. Give a compiler or separation for a specified reduction class.
status: Proposed WE-specific extension beyond Bitansky–Brakerski–Kalai’s nonadaptive theorem. Known superpolynomial-solution-space obstructions exclude an unrestricted conversion claim.
why: Converts successful quantum decryption attacks into witnesses or underlying-assumption attacks.
key_works: Nir Bitansky, Zvika Brakerski, Yael Tauman Kalai (2022), [Constructive Post-Quantum Reductions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02314).

title: Extraction without inverse access to a quantum decryptor
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: Characterize WE relations permitting extraction from forward-only access to a stateful quantum decryptor. Prove query lower bounds or identify additional interfaces needed when inverse-unitary access is unavailable.
status: Proposed interface boundary motivated by quantum rewinding techniques and oracle separations.
why: Separates formal knowledge claims from information recoverable from an externally operated device.
key_works: Andris Ambainis, Ansis Rosmanis, Dominique Unruh (2014), [Quantum Attacks on Classical Proof Systems — The Hardness of Quantum Rewinding](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6898).

title: Prove the needed coset-verifier evasive composability
subfield: Quantum-safe knowledge assumptions for lattice and obfuscation routes
open: Prove joint hiding for the particular coset-authenticated states and differently based ZX-verifier obfuscations used in quantum arguments of knowledge, from ordinary post-quantum iO rather than an additional evasive-composability heuristic.
status: Explicit 2025/2026 open proof step. The unrestricted heuristic has self-referential counterexamples; the construction needs structured samplers.
why: Strengthens quantum proof infrastructure from which QMA condition encryption may be compiled.
key_works: James Bartusek, Ruta Jawale, Justin Raizes, Kabir Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Near-perfect extraction for a fixed quantum verifier
subfield: Extractable QMA conditions and witness representation
open: Extract a witness accepted with probability \(1-\operatorname{negl}(\lambda)\) by the same advertised strongly complete verifier, in polynomial time and without extra input-witness copies, or prove a tight restricted-model barrier.
status: Proposed quality frontier beyond acceptance \(1-\gamma\) for arbitrarily small inverse-polynomial \(\gamma\). Replacing the verifier with an amplified one changes the target.
why: Bounds failure when a scarce extracted witness unlocks many independently issued ciphertexts.
key_works: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Condition encryption with a quantum instance
subfield: Extractable QMA conditions and witness representation
open: Construct nonvacuous WE whose public condition includes bounded copies of an unknown quantum specimen, specifying encryption consumption and witness validity relative to that specimen.
status: Proposed model beyond QMA-WE’s classical instance descriptions. Proofs concerning received quantum states already exist.
why: Supports conditions about physical quantum resources unavailable as classical circuit descriptions.
key_works: Léo Colisson, Frédéric Grosshans, Elham Kashefi (2025), [Non-Interactive and Non-Destructive Zero-Knowledge Proofs on Quantum States and Multi-Party Generation of Authorized Hidden GHZ States](https://doi.org/10.1145/3721487).

title: State-bound confidential firmware rollout
subfield: Software provenance and confidential deployment
open: Release firmware keys only to authorized device states while preserving rollback protection through interrupted installation, recovery, and supplier-key compromise without per-device sender interaction.
status: Proposed 10×-tier lifecycle target. Uptane provides secure-update foundations; WE does not itself certify live state or successful installation.
why: Supports confidential staged distribution to intermittently connected fleets.
key_works: Kuppusamy et al. (2016), [Uptane: Securing Software Updates for Automobiles](https://uptane.org/papers/kuppusamy_escar_16.pdf).

title: Security-parameter-sized prime fields
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Reduce the required prime-field bit length to O(λ+log n), preserving the rank gap and security analysis.
status: Proposed quantitative refinement of the 2026 generic-group construction.
why: Controls arithmetic, encoding, and ciphertext costs.
key_works: Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).
aliases: Small-bitlength field WE; this does not mean polynomial-order cryptographic groups.

title: Tight generic-group witness extraction
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: Determine optimal extractor time and success as functions of adversarial advantage, query count, and witness size.
status: Proposed quantitative frontier beyond October 2026’s polynomial-time extraction claim.
why: Converts existential extractability into concrete application guarantees.
key_works: Campanelli (2026), [A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2399); Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).

title: Remove random-access help in learning-based WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Obtain the learning-to-WE implication with ordinary sample access rather than additional random-access help used by the characterization.
status: Explicit frontier arising from the 2025 learning connection.
why: Aligns the characterization with standard learning interfaces.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Eliminate the half-Levin witness-map requirement
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Recover the learning-to-WE implication from weaker reductions that do not explicitly map satisfying assignments into the required learning witnesses.
status: Proposed strengthening of the 2025 reduction framework.
why: Makes existing NP-hardness reductions potentially usable for WE.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Sublinear indexed positional WE without added LWE
subfield: Offline, batched, positional, and signature-based WE
open: Obtain N^ε-succinct indexed positional WE from plain WE alone, removing the additional LWE premise.
status: The 2026 result establishes an indexed N^ε-succinct construction under combined assumptions; O(N) constructions do not solve this target.
why: Clarifies how much extra power is required to make WE positional.
key_works: Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).

title: Private catch-up for dormant registered receivers
subfield: Permissionless registration and encrypted directories
open: Give dormant receivers private catch-up with polylogarithmic communication and amortized server work, independent of missed registrations, while retaining polylogarithmic registration-update work and publicly verifiable helper correctness.
status: Proposed 1,000×-tier target beyond existing helper-update functionality.
why: Makes encrypted directories usable by intermittently connected devices without hiding a linear server scan.
key_works: Freitag–Waters–Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812).

title: Fully succinct positional WE from ordinary WE and LWE
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: Construct positional WE that compares the entire witness with a secret cutoff, using ordinary NP-WE and LWE, with ciphertext size polynomial in verifier size, security parameter, and witness length. Equivalently, achieve indexed positional WE with polylogarithmic dependence on the index-space size.
status: Proposed frontier sharpened by Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026): their construction has \(N^\varepsilon\) dependence for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) and compares a separate index rather than the full witness.
why: Supports exponentially large ordered witness spaces without exponential ciphertexts.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932); [full version](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).

title: Rate-one null obfuscation below full iO
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: Obtain null-iO with additive size overhead, permitting nested obfuscations without multiplying circuit sizes, from ordinary WE plus LWE. A separation showing that this rate requires substantially stronger primitives would also resolve the target.
status: Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026) identify rate-one null-iO below full iO as a missing ingredient; the specific WE-plus-LWE target is proposed here.
why: Makes deep recursive encryption compilers plausible and isolates whether succinctness increases the assumption strength of null obfuscation.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).

title: Polylogarithmic ciphertexts for publicly traceable registered broadcast
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: From ordinary WE plus LWE, construct registered broadcast-and-trace with public tracing, full collusion resistance, and ciphertext overhead polynomial in \(\lambda\) and \(\log N\). Count recipient-set descriptions separately and retain the existing registration semantics.
status: Proposed parameter target beyond the \(N^\varepsilon\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) ciphertext bound of Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026). Full collusion resistance is already achieved; the missing improvement concerns size.
why: Enables publicly accountable distribution with independently generated subscriber keys at very large population sizes.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).

title: Replace the quantum pseudorandom oracle
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Obtain the QMA-WE consequences of the quantum-pseudorandom-oracle model in the ordinary quantum random-oracle model, or separate the models for this task.
status: The 2025/2026 route uses QPrO; hidden-handle pseudorandom oracles are not ordinary random oracles.
why: Removes a consequential idealization from the construction route.
key_works: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Oracle separation of QMA from QCIP[2]
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Exhibit an oracle, ideally classical, relative to which QMA is not contained in two-message classical-channel quantum interactive proofs.
status: Explicit 2026 next step; separating QMA from QCMA alone is insufficient.
why: Supplies structural evidence for the gap underlying QMA-WE barriers.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), [Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25195).

title: Negligible-disturbance extraction for a live quantum escrow
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: For unique-witness NP relations, extract from quantum EWE adversaries while simulating their residual state jointly with an inaccessible entangled reference, to negligible error in polynomial time.
status: Proposed composition target. Adjustable inverse-polynomial simulation error is established; choosing negligible error can require superpolynomial runtime.
why: Supports subsequent escrow interactions without silently replacing the adversary’s quantum state.
key_works: Nai-Hui Chia, Kai-Min Chung, Xiao Liang, Takashi Yamakawa (2022), [Post-Quantum Simulatable Extraction with Minimal Assumptions: Black-Box and Constant-Round](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08665).

title: A single-copy quantum laconic characterization
subfield: Quantum language classes and witness resources
open: Characterize QMA-WE through laconic proofs while preserving a one-copy quantum-witness budget, or prove that the classical transformation intrinsically needs extra copies.
status: Proposed quantum analogue of the 2026 classical equivalence.
why: Avoids transformations that assume impossible witness duplication.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/); Kalai–Khurana–Raizes (2026), [How to Classically Verify a Quantum Cat without Killing It](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09282).

title: Sublinear setup for black-box pairing registered ABE
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Construct registered ABE for monotone span programs with a structured CRS of \(o(N)\) group elements, using black-box pairing operations and compact aggregated keys, or prove a lower bound in a specified algebraic model. Count every reusable public table as setup.
status: The sublinear-CRS question appears in Wu’s 2024 research agenda. Linear setup for general monotone policies was achieved in 2026; sublinear setup remains distinct.
why: Reduces population-dependent deployment costs without invoking general-purpose WE or obfuscation.
key_works: David J. Wu (2024), [Registration-Based Cryptography](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/talks/RegistrationCrypto0524.pdf); Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Sublinear individual keys with linear registration setup
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Reduce each user’s public key in black-box pairing registered ABE from \(\Theta(N)\) to \(o(N)\) group elements while retaining an \(O(N)\) CRS, general monotone policies, and compact master/helper keys. Prevent the saving from shifting into per-user public auxiliary data.
status: Proposed quantitative target. The 2026 linear-CRS construction retains linear individual public keys.
why: Removes quadratic aggregate upload and storage across a population of \(N\) users.
key_works: Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Linear-CRS pairing registration across independent authorities
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Achieve a CRS linear in supported population for pairing-based multi-authority registered ABE, preserving monotone-span-program policies and independent, non-coordinating curators. State additional dependence on authority count and attribute-universe size explicitly.
status: Proposed target after the 2025 multi-authority construction and 2026 single-authority linear-CRS result; neither establishes the combined guarantee.
why: Makes federated condition encryption less expensive to initialize and maintain.
key_works: George Lu, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2025), [Multi-Authority Registered Attribute-Based Encryption](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredMA-ABE.pdf); Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Sublinear pairing parameters for batched IBE
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Obtain pairing-based batched IBE with \(o(B)\) public-parameter group elements for maximum batch size \(B\), retaining constant-size ciphertexts and batch decryption keys. Establish a lower bound if linear setup is necessary in the specified algebraic model.
status: Explicit May 2026 direction. The subsequent partial-fraction construction still has linear public parameters.
why: Allows large future release sets without setup proportional to their maximum size.
key_works: Gong–Waters–Wee–Wu (2026), [Threshold Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Pairings in the Plain Model](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2103); Dan Boneh, Rohit Nema, Arnab Roy, Ertem Nusret Tas (2026), [Efficient Batch Threshold Encryption Using Partial Fraction Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/674).

title: Additive setup cost for multi-key batched IBE
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Support \(q\) decryption-key queries per label and batches of size \(B\) with CRS size \(\widetilde O(B+q)\), rather than \(O(qB)\), retaining constant-size ciphertexts and compact release keys. Require security for overlapping adversarially chosen release sets.
status: Proposed quantitative target after Policharla (July 2026), which establishes multi-key-per-label feasibility with an \(O(qB)\) CRS.
why: Prevents repeated releases from multiplying the setup burden.
key_works: Guru-Vamsi Policharla (2026), [Labeled Multi-Key Batched IBE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1452).

title: Compact batched IBE from plain LWE
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Replace succinct LWE with plain LWE in standard-model batched IBE while keeping master public keys, ciphertexts, and batch keys polynomial in \(\lambda\) and \(\log B\). Specify the required modulus-to-noise ratio.
status: Proposed assumption-reduction target after Xiong–Zhang–Chen (2026), which gives standard-model lattice batched IBE from succinct LWE using compact inner-product encryption with decomposable key generation.
why: Gives quantum-resistant bulk conditional release a special-language route independent of general NP-WE.
key_works: Saisi Xiong, Yijian Zhang, Jie Chen (2026), [Efficient Batched IBE from Lattices in the Standard Model](https://cic.iacr.org/p/3/2/18); [DOI 10.62056/aksude-3](https://doi.org/10.62056/aksude-3).

title: Adaptive evolving mNP sharing with short immutable shares
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: From ordinary WE plus LWE, give adaptive privacy for all rigid, efficiently described evolving mNP policies without knowing the final population or future evolution. Keep old shares immutable, each new share \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n,\log|V_n|)\) bits, and cumulative per-secret public payload \(O(n\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|V_n|))\) while arrivals and corruptions interleave.
status: Proposed strengthening of Francati–Giammusso–Venturi (2025/2026). Evolving mNP sharing and adaptive evolving monotone-circuit sharing exist; inherited succinctness from succinct WE does not establish these bounds from ordinary WE.
why: Supports institutions accepting new participants for decades without recalling all existing shares.
key_works: Danilo Francati, Sara Giammusso, Daniele Venturi (2025/2026), [Taming Adaptive Security and New Access Structures in Evolving Secret Sharing](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-95-5125-5_3).

title: Succinct traceable sharing for witness access structures
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Add non-frameable black-box tracing to succinct mNP sharing with \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n)\)-bit private shares and near-linear public data plus a succinct verifier term. Use nonvacuous general-access tracing games, including unauthorized stored and supplementary coalitions whose union is authorized, with explicit query distributions and success thresholds.
status: Proposed quantitative target beyond Goyal–Jain–Partap’s corrected constructions and security tradeoffs. Their work shows that earlier tracing definitions can become vacuous for general access structures.
why: Makes private conditional decryption authority accountable when participants sell reconstruction services.
key_works: Vipul Goyal, Abhishek Jain, Aditi Partap (2025/2026), [Traceable Secret Sharing Revisited](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1980); Oriol Farràs, Miquel Guiot (2025/2026), [Traceable Secret Sharing Schemes for General Access Structures](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1120).

title: Plain-to-extractable WE for controlled instance distributions
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Derive extractable security from plain WE for independently sampled hard NP-search distributions, with instance-independent adversarial advice and explicit extractor access, without adding a knowledge assumption.
status: Proposed compiler frontier. False-instance security gives no generic hard-true guarantee; unrestricted auxiliary input encounters conditional barriers.
why: Could justify theorem and event rewards under weaker premises.
key_works: Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).

title: Separate ordinary WE from general obfuscation
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Determine whether general WE is strictly weaker than iO under arbitrary constructions, or derive iO from WE and explicitly identified weaker primitives.
status: Open since 2013. Black-box barriers and 2026 indexed positional-WE results do not settle arbitrary reductions.
why: Determines whether condition encryption inherits the full difficulty of program obfuscation.
key_works: Garg–Mahmoody–Mohammed (2017), [Lower Bounds on Obfuscation from All-or-Nothing Encryption Primitives](https://momahmoody.github.io/files/papers/IO-all-or-nothing.pdf); Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).

title: Statistical WE versus smooth projective hashing
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Determine whether every statistically secure WE relation admits a comparably efficient smooth projective hash system, or exhibit a separating relation.
status: Projective hashing supplies one direction; the 2026 laconic characterization provides a different proof-system perspective.
why: Identifies whether projective hashing exhausts useful information-theoretic witness encryption.
key_works: Cramer–Shoup (2002), [Universal Hash Proofs and a Paradigm for Adaptive Chosen Ciphertext Secure Public-Key Encryption](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-46035-7_4); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Statistical WE throughout efficiently witnessed SZK
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Characterize languages in NP∩SZK admitting statistical WE with efficient decryption from their designated NP witnesses.
status: Proposed classification beyond the established characterization through laconic special-honest-verifier statistical zero knowledge.
why: Locates conditions whose ciphertext secrecy survives unlimited adversarial computation.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: The superlogarithmic laconicity boundary
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Determine the greatest prover-communication bound from which efficient WE follows, or prove a threshold separating logarithmic and superlogarithmic protocols.
status: Proposed boundary question after the 2026 characterization; direct transcript enumeration becomes superpolynomial beyond logarithmic communication.
why: Clarifies whether slightly longer arguments remain sufficient.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Unconditional half-Levin NP-hardness of improper learning
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Establish the relevant NP-hardness of improper learning through witness-preserving half-Levin reductions without assuming WE.
status: The 2025 characterization identifies a strong connection; unconditional hardness would provide corresponding cryptographic consequences.
why: Turns a learning-theoretic hardness theorem into a route toward conditional encryption.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Unconditional WE against restricted adversaries
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Construct meaningful WE secure against an explicit restricted adversary class using unconditional circuit or learning lower bounds.
status: Identified as a direction in 2025; the adversary restriction must leave a nontrivial decryption and security problem.
why: Could provide unconditional prototypes and reveal the computational source of WE hardness.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Uniform-example-distribution learning characterization
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Characterize WE through learning hardness under a fixed uniform example distribution, or isolate the necessity of more general distributions.
status: Proposed restriction of the 2025 equivalence.
why: Connects WE to central distribution-specific learning problems.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Uniform versus nonuniform WE power
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Determine which implications of WE survive when security and reductions are restricted to uniform algorithms, and separate uniform from nonuniform formulations where possible.
status: The 2025 learning results expose consequential nonuniformity requirements.
why: Prevents advice assumptions from silently strengthening cryptographic conclusions.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Cryptographic consequences of uniform-only WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Establish the strongest encryption and one-wayness consequences of WE secure only against uniform attackers under explicit uniform complexity assumptions.
status: Proposed clarification; existing results differ in uniformity, all-input security, and hardness premises.
why: Separates necessary computational assumptions from proof artifacts.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2025), [A Note on Zero-Knowledge for NP and One-Way Functions](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/095/revision/2/download).

title: Remove auxiliary circuit hardness from short-WE consequences
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Derive the relevant short-WE/GapDistMCSP relationship without the additional hardness assumption for exponential-time computation against circuits.
status: Proposed assumption-removal target in the 2025 meta-complexity connection.
why: Isolates whether succinct WE itself explains the resulting hardness.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: A WE-only barrier to Levin hardness of GapMCSP
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Identify the weakest WE premise sufficient to obstruct appropriate Levin reductions proving NP-hardness of GapMCSP.
status: Existing meta-complexity barriers use particular cryptographic or reduction hypotheses; removing additional premises remains the target.
why: Explains why natural completeness strategies may fail.
key_works: Mazor–Pass (2024), [CCC 2024 paper](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.36); Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: WE-induced barriers for learning reductions
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Classify which witness-preserving, randomized, adaptive, or oracle learning reductions are incompatible with specified forms of WE.
status: Proposed extension of the 2024–2025 meta-complexity and learning barriers.
why: Directs learning-hardness efforts toward reduction types that remain viable.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); Mazor–Pass (2024), [CCC 2024 paper](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.36).

title: Polynomial-security WE for strong conditional-Kolmogorov hardness
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Obtain the strongest known approximation-hardness consequences for time-bounded conditional Kolmogorov complexity from polynomially secure WE.
status: Proposed weakening of cryptographic hardness requirements in the 2023/2025 line of work.
why: Connects conventional security levels to quantitative meta-complexity.
key_works: Huang–Ilango–Ren (2023/2025), [paper on conditional Kolmogorov complexity](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M1608483).

title: Near-input-length time bounds for conditional description hardness
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Extend WE-derived conditional-Kolmogorov approximation hardness to time bounds close to the input length while preserving a meaningful approximation gap.
status: Proposed quantitative frontier; time bounds and reduction overhead are substantive restrictions.
why: Makes the connection relevant to efficient compression and prediction.
key_works: Huang–Ilango–Ren (2023/2025), [paper on conditional Kolmogorov complexity](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M1608483).

title: Nondeterministically secure WE from conventional assumptions
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Construct the stronger WE security needed against nondeterministic distinguishers from well-studied assumptions, with explicit circuit and advice bounds.
status: Strong WE supplies range-avoidance consequences; a conventional-assumption foundation remains a separate target.
why: Could establish new search and proof-complexity lower bounds.
key_works: Chen–Li (2023/2024), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Remote Point for Restricted Circuits via Cryptography](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/206/); Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061).

title: Expressivity limits of nondeterministic WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Determine which language classes and cryptographic consequences are possible under nondeterministic WE security, and prove separations from ordinary WE.
status: Proposed classification target motivated by recent range-avoidance applications.
why: Clarifies whether a strong assumption has narrow applications or broad structural consequences.
key_works: Chen–Li (2023/2024), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Remote Point for Restricted Circuits via Cryptography](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/206/); Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061).

title: Compact public validity with unique decryption
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Add succinct public ciphertext-validity verification and robust unique decryption without imposing full general-purpose proof overhead.
status: Basic unique-decryption WE is already studied and constructed; compact publicly checkable validity is the stronger target.
why: Prevents ambiguous or malformed encrypted rewards.
key_works: Niu–Li–Huang–Liang–Tang (2015), [paper on unique-decryption WE](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-17533-1_38); Pan–Liang–Li–Ni (2019), [subsequent WE construction](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-21548-4_33).

title: Selective opening for condition portfolios
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Prove security when an adversary adaptively opens some ciphertexts, learns their witnesses and randomness, and attacks correlated unopened conditions.
status: Proposed WE-specific composition target; ordinary indistinguishability does not establish selective-opening security.
why: Supports portfolios of related escrows and archives.
key_works: Bellare–Dowsley–Waters–Yilek (2011), [selective-opening encryption research](https://eprint.iacr.org/2011/581); Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704).

title: Tight multi-instance adaptive soundness
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Obtain tight security under adaptively selected, correlated instances and many ciphertexts without losses proportional to every possible challenge position.
status: Adaptive WE is established; tight quantitative composition remains the proposed frontier.
why: Enables large services without excessive parameter inflation.
key_works: Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704).

title: Ciphertext-size lower bounds
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Prove ciphertext-size lower bounds as functions of relation description, witness length, batch count, and security model, separating universal from indexed settings.
status: Proposed lower-bound program sharpened by recent succinct batch and positional constructions.
why: Distinguishes engineering inefficiency from inherent representation cost.
key_works: Devadas–Jain–Waters–Wu (2025/2026), [Succinct Witness Encryption for Batch Languages and Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/944).

title: A machine-checked WE definition lattice
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Formalize WE definitions and implication proofs, including adaptive, extractable, statistical, succinct, and quantum variants, with explicit failed converses.
status: Proposed infrastructure target; substantial distinctions currently reside across separate papers.
why: Prevents applications from assuming guarantees their primitive does not provide.
key_works: Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/).

title: A witness-preserving reduction corpus

title: Reproduction-gated scientific data release

open: Unlock artifacts after certificates verify declared computations on authenticated inputs, with precise provenance and acceptance rules.
status: Proposed 10×-tier target; computational reproduction does not certify truthful physical measurement.
why: Links data access to reproducible scientific work.
key_works: Gennaro et al. (2010), [Non-Interactive Verifiable Computing: Outsourcing Computation to Untrusted Workers](https://eprint.iacr.org/2009/547).

title: Independently replicated-result thresholds
subfield: Scientific release, consent, archives, and optimization
open: Release funds or data after replication certificates under a defensible independence model, quantifying shared-method and shared-data correlations.
status: Proposed experimental target; threshold credentials do not establish independent experiments.
why: Prevents correlated replications from creating false confidence.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2016), [Town Crier: An Authenticated Data Feed for Smart Contracts](https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/168).

title: Preregistered release without selective omission
subfield: Scientific release, consent, archives, and optimization
open: Commit complete analysis and release plans before outcomes and prove every required result was included, including unfavorable ones.
status: Proposed target; timestamps and execution proofs separately do not prove complete publication.
why: Prevents conditional-release infrastructure from reinforcing publication bias.
key_works: Haber–Stornetta (1991), [How to Time-Stamp a Digital Document](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-38424-3_32).

title: Statistically valid adaptive release conditions
subfield: Scientific release, consent, archives, and optimization
open: Bound false-release probability under repeated testing, optional stopping, and adaptive hypotheses, binding procedures and access histories to witnesses.
status: Proposed 1,000×-tier target; verified computation cannot repair invalid statistical inference.
why: Makes automated evidence thresholds scientifically defensible.
key_works: Howard et al. (2021), [Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.08240).

title: Consent-scoped release with prospective withdrawal
subfield: Scientific release, consent, archives, and optimization
open: Release only records whose authenticated consent permits specified recipients and computations at finalized epochs, hiding unrelated policies and identities.
status: Proposed target; withdrawal governs future access and cannot recall plaintext already released.
why: Supports precise conditional access to sensitive datasets.
key_works: Faust et al. (2023), [Statement-Oblivious Threshold Witness Encryption](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/668).

title: Training-data access with verifiable usage receipts
subfield: Scientific release, consent, archives, and optimization
open: Condition access on authorized computations while explicitly separating provable execution from promises about retained plaintext or later models.
status: Proposed physics-limit target; downstream confinement needs hardware, MPC, or service assumptions beyond WE.
why: Defines useful, technically enforceable data-use agreements.
key_works: Gennaro et al. (2010), [Non-Interactive Verifiable Computing: Outsourcing Computation to Untrusted Workers](https://eprint.iacr.org/2009/547).

title: Self-describing conditional archives
subfield: Scientific release, consent, archives, and optimization
open: Preserve enough executable and mathematical specification to reimplement future release verifiers and check consistency with ciphertexts and migration certificates.
status: Proposed 10×-tier archival target; surviving bytes and timestamps are insufficient.
why: Makes conditionally encrypted knowledge interpretable across generations.
key_works: Haber–Stornetta (1991), [How to Time-Stamp a Digital Document](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-38424-3_32).

title: Optimization-certificate reward ladders
subfield: Scientific release, consent, archives, and optimization
open: Reward improved feasible solutions and certified bounds while preventing equivalent repeat claims, using tractable certificate classes.
status: Proposed 1,000×-tier target; faster WE does not make every global-optimality claim NP-verifiable.
why: Creates continuous incentives for measurable optimization progress.
key_works: Kumaresan–Bentov (2014), [How to Use Bitcoin to Incentivize Correct Computations](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/use-bitcoin-incentivize-correct-computations/).
